(basketball)|Rebounds]] | stat2value = 6,604 (7.4 rpg) | stat3label = [[Assist (basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 2,996 (3.4 apg) | stats_league = NBA }} '''Marc Gasol Sáez''' ({{IPA|ca|ˈmaɾɡ ɡəˈzɔl|lang}}, {{IPA|es|ˈmaɾk gaˈsol|lang}}; born 29 January 1985) is a Spanish former professional [[basketball]] player who is the president of [[Bàsquet Girona]] of the [[Liga ACB]]. The [[Center (basketball)|center]] is a two-time [[All-NBA Team]] member and a three-time [[NBA All-Star]]. He was named the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year]] with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in 2013, and won an [[NBA championship]] with the [[Toronto Raptors]] in 2019. Gasol was drafted 48th overall by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the [[2007 NBA draft]]. After having his rights traded to Memphis in February 2008 in a deal that sent his older brother [[Pau Gasol]] to the Lakers, he signed with the Grizzlies and remained with the franchise until being traded to Toronto in 2019. He rejoined the Lakers in 2020 for one season. Gasol has been a regular member of the [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain national team]] since 2006. He has won two [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Olympic]] silver medals and two [[FIBA Basketball World Cup]] titles. In the [[EuroBasket]], he has won two titles, a silver medal, and two bronze medals. ==Early life== Gasol was born and raised in [[Barcelona]], Spain. In 2001, he moved as a teenager with his parents to the [[Memphis, Tennessee|Memphis]] suburb of [[Germantown, Tennessee]], after his older brother [[Pau Gasol|Pau]] joined the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. Gasol played high school basketball at [[Lausanne Collegiate School]] in Memphis.{{cite magazine |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1167642/2/index.htm |title=The power of Pau |last=Jenkins |first=Lee |date=March 29, 2010 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |page=2 2012 |url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== [[File:Marc Gasol.JPG|thumb|left|200px|Gasol with [[CB Sant Josep|Girona]] in May 2008]] ===FC Barcelona (2003–2006)=== After graduating from Lausanne, Gasol returned to his home country of Spain to play in the [[Liga ACB]] for [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]]. ===CB Girona (2006–2008)=== After three seasons with Barcelona, Gasol signed with [[CB Sant Josep|Girona]] in 2006. In 2008, he was named the [[ACB Most Valuable Player Award|ACB Most Valuable Player]]. ===Memphis Grizzlies (2008–2019)=== ====Early years==== Gasol was selected by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] with the 48th overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]]. On February 1, 2008, his draft rights were traded by the Lakers to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] as part of a trade package that included his older brother, [[Pau Gasol|Pau]], who was sent from the Grizzlies to the Lakers.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/080201gasol_trade.html |title=Lakers Acquire Gasol From Grizzlies |work=NBA.com |date=February 1, 2008 |access-date=November 16, 2018}}{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_trade_gasol_to_lakers-080201.html |title=Grizzlies trade Pau Gasol to Lakers for four players and two first round picks |work=NBA.com |date=February 1, 2008 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} On July 9, 2008, he signed with the Grizzlies.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_sign_marc_gasol-080709.html |title=Grizzlies sign 2008 ACB Most Valuable Player Marc Gasol |work=NBA.com |date=July 9, 2008 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} He set a franchise rookie record for field goal percentage in a season with 53 percent. The previous record was held by Pau with 51.8 percent in 2001–02.{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290415029 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181117151443/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290415029 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 17, 2018 |title=Grizzlies take advantage of Hawks reserves |work=ESPN.com |date=April 15, 2009 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} He subsequently earned [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] honors.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/allstar/2012/players/marc_gasol.html |title=Player Profile: Marc Gasol |work=NBA.com |access-date=November 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120217232306/http://www.nba.com/allstar/2012/players/marc_gasol.html |archive-date=February 17, 2012 |url-status=dead}} After averaging 11.9 points and 7.4 rebounds as a rookie, he averaged 14.6 points and 9.3 rebounds in 2009–10 with a career-best .581 field goal percentage.{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gasolma01.html |title=Marc Gasol |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=November 16, 2018}} The 2010–11 season saw Gasol average 11.7 points, 7.0 rebounds, a career-high 2.5 assists and 1.68 blocks in 81 games (all starts). He then posted 15.0 points, 11.2 rebounds, 2.2 assists, and 2.15 blocks in helping lead the Grizzlies through a 13-game run in the [[2011 NBA Playoffs]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_re-sign_gasol-111214 |title=Grizzlies re-sign Gasol to multi-year contract |work=NBA.com |date=December 14, 2011 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} Memphis, which had never even won a playoff game before 2011, defeated the Western Conference's top-seeded [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the opening round, then went to a deciding seventh game against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7353554/report-memphis-grizzlies-re-sign-marc-gasol-four-years-nearly-58-million |title=Memphis Grizzlies re-sign Marc Gasol |work=ESPN.com |date=December 14, 2011 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} Gasol led the Grizzlies in field goal accuracy and blocked shots in each of his first three NBA seasons. ====2011–12 season: First All-Star selection==== On December 14, 2011, Gasol re-signed with the Grizzlies to a four-year, $58 million contract. On January 23, 2012, he was named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played January 16–22.{{cite web |url=http://pr.nba.com/dwight-howard-marc-gasol-nba-players-of-the-week/ |title=Magic's Dwight Howard, Grizzlies' Marc Gasol named NBA Players of the Week |work=NBA.com |date=January 23, 2012 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} On February 9, 2012, he was named an [[NBA All-Star]] for the first time, earning a place on the Western Conference roster as a reserve for the [[2012 NBA All-Star Game]].{{cite web |url=http://origin.nba.com/2012/allstar/2012/02/09/reserves-release/ |title=Pierce, Nowitzki headline reserves for 2012 All-Star Game |work=NBA.com |date=February 9, 2012 |access-date=November 16, 2018 |archive-date=August 29, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190829033738/http://origin.nba.com/2012/allstar/2012/02/09/reserves-release/ |url-status=dead }} ====2012–13 season: Defensive Player of the Year==== In 2012–13, Gasol was one of only six players to average at least 1.5 blocks (1.7 bpg) and 1.0 steals (1.0 spg). He led a Grizzlies defense that allowed a league-low 88.7 points per game during the regular season. His +5.4 score differential ranked second among NBA centers; additionally, Memphis enjoyed a +7.5 score differential when Gasol was on the court compared with -3.9 when he was on the bench.{{cite web |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |title=Grizzlies' Gasol named Kia Defensive Player of the Year |date=April 24, 2013 |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/04/24/grizzlies-marc-gasol-named-kia-defensive-player-of-the-year/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130427002829/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/04/24/grizzlies-marc-gasol-named-kia-defensive-player-of-the-year/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpts |archive-date=April 27, 2013 |url-status=live}} In April 2013, he was named the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award|NBA Defensive Player of the Year]], becoming the first player in Grizzlies history to earn the honour, the first Spanish man to win, and the first European to win. [[ESPN]] lauded the Grizzlies' ability to force turnovers with Gasol on the court anchoring the defense.{{cite news |last=Saini |first=Sunny |title=Gasol's stingy defense earns award |date=April 24, 2013 |publisher=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/statsinfo/post/_/id/64910/64910 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130425073129/http://espn.go.com/blog/statsinfo/post/_/id/64910/64910 |archive-date=April 25, 2013 |url-status=live}} He was also named to the [[All-NBA Second Team]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/13/all-defensive-team-official-release/ |title=Allen, James headline 2012-13 NBA All-Defensive First Team |work=NBA.com |date=May 13, 2013 |access-date=November 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026043439/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/13/all-defensive-team-official-release/ |archive-date=October 26, 2013 |url-status=dead}} Despite winning Defensive Player of the Year, Gasol was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] due to a different voting system.{{cite web |last=Joseph |first=Adi |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2013/05/13/2012-13-all-defensive-team-voting-marc-gasol-lebron-james-tony-allen/2156007/ |title=Marc Gasol left off LeBron James-led all-defensive team |work=USA Today |date=May 13, 2013 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} ====2013–14 season: MCL injury==== [[File:Marc Gasol backs in to Blake Griffin 20131118 Clippers v Grizzles (cropped).jpg|thumb|Gasol in November 2013, backing down [[Blake Griffin]]]] In 2013–14, Gasol played a career-low 59 games. A left [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] sprain suffered on November 22 against the [[San Antonio Spurs]]{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131122/SASMEM/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Spurs 102, Grizzlies 86 |work=NBA.com |date=November 22, 2013 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} sidelined him for 23 games from November 25 to January 12.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140114/OKCMEM/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Grizzlies 90, Thunder 87 |work=NBA.com |date=January 14, 2014 |access-date=November 16, 2018 |quote=Grizzlies' center Marc Gasol made a surprising return to the lineup after missing seven weeks with a left MCL sprain.}}{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gasolma01/gamelog/2014/ |title=Marc Gasol 2013-14 Game Log |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=November 16, 2018}} ====2014–15 season: All-NBA First Team selection==== The 2014–15 season saw Gasol earn his second [[NBA All-Star]] selection, earning his first All-Star start, and was named to the [[All-NBA First Team]] for the first time.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/05/21/2014-15-all-nba-first-team-official-release/ |title=Warriors' Curry and Cavaliers' James unanimous picks for 2014-15 All-NBA First Team |work=NBA.com |date=May 21, 2015 |access-date=May 21, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160723034332/http://www.nba.com/2015/news/05/21/2014-15-all-nba-first-team-official-release |archive-date=July 23, 2016 |url-status=dead}} He averaged a career-best 17.4 points to go with 7.8 rebounds and 3.8 assists for the 55-win Grizzlies. He scored 30-plus points five times after doing so just once in his first six seasons. He set career-highs in field goals made and attempted, as well as free throws made and attempted. He was the only player in the league with at least 1,300 points, 600 rebounds, and 300 assists.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-resign-marc-gasol-150713 |title=Memphis Grizzlies re-sign All-NBA First Team Center Marc Gasol |work=NBA.com |date=July 13, 2015 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} ====2015–16 season: Contract extension==== On July 13, 2015, Gasol re-signed with the Grizzlies on a five-year maximum contract worth an estimated $110 million.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13251148/marc-gasol-signs-5-year-deal-staying-memphis-grizzlies |title=Marc Gasol signs 5-year deal to stay in Memphis, Grizzlies announce |work=ESPN.com |date=July 13, 2015 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} On November 20, he recorded his first career triple-double with 16 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists in a 96–84 win over the [[Houston Rockets]], marking the first triple-double for Memphis since 2007 when his brother Pau recorded 17 points, 13 rebounds, and 12 assists.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151120/HOUMEM/gameinfo.html |title=Conley, Gasol lead Grizzlies over Rockets 96-84 |work=NBA.com |date=November 20, 2015 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} Gasol set a new career low for games played with 52 after missing the second half of the season with a broken right foot.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/gasol-injury-update-160209 |title=Marc Gasol injury update |work=NBA.com |date=February 9, 2016 |access-date=November 16, 2018}}{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/gasol-injury-update-160223 |title=Marc Gasol Injury Update |work=NBA.com |date=February 23, 2016 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} ====2016–17 season: Career high in scoring==== [[File:Marc Gasol 20131118 Clippers v Grizzles (cropped).jpg|200px|thumb|left|Gasol in November 2013]] On December 5, 2016, Gasol recorded his second career triple-double with 28 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists in a 110–108 double-overtime win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899752 |title=Gasol, Grizzlies outlast Pelicans, 110-108 in double OT |work=ESPN.com |date=December 5, 2016 |access-date=December 6, 2016}} On December 12, he was named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played December 5–11. It marked his second career Player of the Week award and the ninth time a Grizzlies player has won the weekly accolade.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/gasol-western-player-of-the-week-161212 |title=Marc Gasol named Western Conference Player of the Week |work=NBA.com |date=December 12, 2016 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} On January 25, 2017, he scored a career-high 42 points in a 101–99 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900106 |title=Gasol scores a career-high 42 to lead Grizzlies past Raptors |work=ESPN.com |date=January 25, 2017 |access-date=January 26, 2017}} A day later, he was named an [[NBA All-Star]] for the third time in his career.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/01/26/2017-all-star-reserves-official-release |title=Thunder's Westbrook and three first-time All-Stars headline reserves for 2017 NBA All-Star Game |work=NBA.com |date=January 26, 2017 |access-date=November 17, 2018}}{{cite web |last=Whitaker |first=Lang |url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/01/26/nba-all-star-reserves-2017-revealed |title=Warriors, Cavaliers dominate selections for NBA All-Star 2017 as reserves are revealed |work=NBA.com |date=January 26, 2017 |access-date=November 17, 2018}} On March 16, 2017, he recorded his third career triple-double with 18 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 103–91 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900412 |title=Gasol's triple-double helps Grizzlies top Hawks 103-91 |work=ESPN.com |date=March 16, 2017 |access-date=March 17, 2017}} ====2017–18 season: 10,000 points==== On December 2, 2017, Gasol passed 10,000 career points with 27 points in a 116–111 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975080 |title=James takes over as Cavaliers win 11th straight |work=ESPN.com |date=December 2, 2017 |access-date=December 2, 2017}} On January 26, 2018, Gasol recorded his fourth career triple-double with 13 points, 12 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 109–100 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975464 |title=Williams has 40 points,10 assists, Clippers beat Grizzlies |work=ESPN.com |date=January 26, 2018 |access-date=January 26, 2018}} In February 2018, Gasol played his 700th career NBA game and made his 689th start, surpassing [[Mike Conley Jr.]] for the most games started in franchise history.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975644 |title=Irving scores 25, Celtics hold off Grizzlies 109-98 |work=ESPN.com |date=February 26, 2018 |access-date=February 26, 2018}} ====2018–19 season: Final season in Memphis==== In November 2018, Gasol passed [[Zach Randolph]] (5,612) to become the Grizzlies' all-time career rebound leader.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070901 |title=Jackson, Gasol lead Grizzlies past Kings 112-104 |work=ESPN.com |date=November 16, 2018 |access-date=November 16, 2018}} In December, Gasol made at least one 3-pointer in 13 consecutive games, which tied a career-high.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071207 |title=Irving, Horford lead rally as Celtics beat Grizzlies 112-103 |work=ESPN.com |date=December 29, 2018 |access-date=December 30, 2018 |quote=Gasol has made a 3-pointer in 12 consecutive games, one short of his career-best 13 in December 2017.}}{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071220 |title=Harden's 43 points, triple-double lead Rockets over Memphis |work=ESPN.com |date=December 31, 2018 |access-date=January 1, 2019 |quote=Gasol has at least one 3-pointer in 13 consecutive games, which ties a career high.}} He set a new record in the first game of January, making a 3-pointer in his 14th straight game on January 2 against the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071236 |title=Griffin's 26 points leads Pistons past Grizzlies 101-94 |work=ESPN.com |date=January 2, 2019 |access-date=January 3, 2019 |quote=Gasol has made a 3-pointer in 14 consecutive games, eclipsing the longest such streak of his career in December of 2017.}} The streak ended at 15 games.{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gasolma01/gamelog/2019/ |title=Marc Gasol 2018-19 Game Log |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=January 8, 2019}} On January 23, he recorded his fifth career triple-double with 22 points, 17 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 118–107 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071386 |title=Walker, Batum lead Hornets over the Grizzlies 118-107 |work=ESPN.com |date=January 23, 2019 |access-date=January 24, 2019}} This would end nearly two decades of a Gasol brother being on the Grizzlies roster. ===Toronto Raptors (2019–2020)=== [[File:1 marc gasol toronto raptors 2019 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|Gasol with the Raptors in 2019]] On February 7, 2019, Gasol was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[C. J. Miles]], [[Jonas Valančiūnas]], [[Delon Wright]] and a 2024 second-round draft pick.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-acquire-gasol-from-grizzlies |title=Raptors Acquire Gasol From Grizzlies |work=NBA.com |date=February 7, 2019 |access-date=February 7, 2019}} He made his debut for the Raptors two days later, recording seven points and six rebounds in 19 minutes off the bench in a 104–99 win over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071501 |title=Gasol pitches in, Raptors send Knicks to 16th loss in row |work=ESPN.com |date=February 9, 2019 |access-date=February 10, 2019}} Gasol soon stepped into the starting center role in Toronto, and his pass-first offensive approach helped the Raptors become the NBA's top 3-point shooting team over the second half of the season.{{cite web |last=Cobb |first=David |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/nba/grizzlies/2019/06/13/grizzlies-legend-marc-gasol-wins-nba-championship-toronto-raptors/1409675001/ |title=Marc Gasol thanks Grizzlies teammates after winning NBA championship with Toronto Raptors |work=commercialappeal.com |date=June 13, 2019 |access-date=June 16, 2019}} He helped the Raptors reach the [[2019 NBA Finals]]. In his first ever NBA Finals game, Gasol scored 20 points and grabbed 7 rebounds in a win.{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201905300TOR.html |title=Golden State Warriors at Toronto Raptors Box Score, May 30, 2019 |publisher=Basketball-Reference |date=May 30, 2019 |access-date=July 28, 2020}} After defeating the [[Golden State Warriors]] in six games, Marc joined his brother Pau, and his two championships in 2009 and 2010, as the first set of brothers to win NBA titles.{{cite web |last=Zemek |first=Matthew |url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba-finals-news-marc-gasol-pau-gasol-become-first-brothers-to-win-championship/ |title=Marc Gasol, Pau Gasol become first brothers to win NBA championship |work=clutchpoints.com |date=June 14, 2019 |access-date=June 16, 2019}} On June 26, 2019, Gasol opted in with the Toronto Raptors by exercising his $25.6 million player option for the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 season]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/06/26/raptors-marc-gasol-accepts-player-option |title=Raptors' Gasol accepts one-year player option |work=NBA.com |date=June 26, 2019 |access-date=June 26, 2019}} On November 25, 2019, despite only scoring 3 points, Gasol had his best game of the season with 6 rebounds and 9 assists while holding [[Joel Embiid]] scoreless for the first time in his career in a 101–96 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. ===Los Angeles Lakers (2020–2021)=== On November 24, 2020, Gasol signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |title=Lakers Sign Marc Gasol |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-marc-gasol |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 25, 2020 |date=November 24, 2020}} On December 22, he made his Lakers debut, going scoreless while putting up one rebound and one assist in a 116–109 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web |url=https://www.silverscreenandroll.com/2020/12/23/22198277/lakers-marc-gasol-disappointing-regular-season-debut-frank-vogel-comments-practice-report |title=Marc Gasol is determined to bounce back from his disappointing debut |website=SB Nation |last=Rivas |first=Christian |access-date=December 29, 2020 |date=December 22, 2020}}{{cite web |url=https://lakersnation.com/marc-gasol-play-can-only-get-better-after-rough-lakers-debut/2020/12/25/ |title=Marc Gasol Confident Play 'Can Only Get Better' After Rough Lakers Debut |website=Lakers Nation |last=Gutterman |first=Ron |access-date=December 29, 2020 |date=December 25, 2020}} Gasol missed nine games mid-season when he contracted [[COVID-19]].{{Cite web |last=Weinstein |first=Josh |title=Vogel: Gasol to return from 9-game absence on minutes limit |url=https://www.thescore.com/nba/news/2138444 |access-date=April 16, 2021 |website=theScore.com|date=March 25, 2021 }}{{Cite magazine |last=Williams |first=Eric D. |date=March 25, 2021 |title=Lakers center Marc Gasol set for return vs. Sixers |url=https://www.si.com/nba/lakers/news/la-lakers-center-marc-gasol-set-to-return-vs-sixers |access-date=April 16, 2021 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}} He was moved to the bench after the team acquired [[Andre Drummond]].{{cite news |first=Dan |last=Woike |title=Marc Gasol: Lakers signing Andre Drummond a 'hard pill to swallow' |date=April 2, 2021 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2021-04-02/marc-gasol-andre-drummond-trade-lakers-demotion |access-date=April 3, 2021}}{{Cite web |last=Faigen |first=Harrison |date=April 1, 2021 |title=Wesley Matthews says Lakers have 'nothing but respect' for how Marc Gasol has handled benching |url=https://www.silverscreenandroll.com/2021/4/1/22361837/lakers-bench-marc-gasol-andre-drummond-wesley-matthews-frank-vogel-rotation |access-date=April 16, 2021 |website=Silver Screen and Roll}} On April 6, 2021, Gasol had 13 points, 9 rebounds, 5 assists, and 4 blocks in a Lakers 110–101 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{Cite web |title=Lakers' Marc Gasol: Torches former team |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/lakers-marc-gasol-torches-former-team/ |access-date=April 16, 2021 |website=CBSSports.com|date=April 7, 2021 }} He started 42 games during the regular season but missed 20 others. In 19.1 minutes per game, he averaged 5.0 points and 4.1 rebounds while attempting 2.3 three-pointer per game, making 41.0%. In the postseason, the Lakers were up 2–1 in the first round against the [[Phoenix Suns]], before losing three straight games and exiting the playoffs in six games. Trying to stave off elimination, the Lakers moved Gasol back into the starting lineup in Game 6, where he was scoreless but finished with seven assists in 18 minutes.{{cite news |first=Phil |last=Watson |title=Los Angeles Lakers Have a Big Problem Looming With Training Camp Fast Approaching |date=August 24, 2021 |work=Sportscasting |url=https://www.sportscasting.com/los-angeles-lakers-have-a-big-problem-looming-camp/ |access-date=September 11, 2021}}{{cite news |first=Dan |last=Woike |title=Lakers trade Marc Gasol to the Grizzlies |date=September 10, 2021 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2021-09-10/lakers-trade-marc-gasol-to-memphis-grizzlies |access-date=September 11, 2021}} During the offseason, the Lakers signed centers [[Dwight Howard]] and [[DeAndre Jordan]]. On September 10, 2021, Gasol was traded back to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] along with a 2024 second round pick in exchange for the draft rights to [[Wang Zhelin]],{{cite web |title=Grizzlies Complete Trade with Lakers |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-complete-trade-with-lakers-210910 |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 10, 2021 |date=September 10, 2021}} saving the Lakers over $10 million in [[NBA luxury tax|luxury-tax]] penalties; however, he was waived five days later by the Grizzlies.{{cite web |title=Grizzlies waive Marc Gasol |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-waive-marc-gasol-210915 |website=NBA.com |date=September 15, 2021 |access-date=September 15, 2021}} ===Bàsquet Girona (2021–2023)=== [[File:Marc Gasol 2022 Girona (cropped).png|thumb|upright|Gasol with [[Bàsquet Girona|Girona]] in 2022]] On November 25, 2021, Gasol announced that he would play for [[Bàsquet Girona]] of the [[Liga Española de Baloncesto|LEB Oro]], the club that he founded, until the end of the [[2021–22 LEB Oro season|2021–22 season]].{{Cite web |title=Marc Gasol to play for Spanish club Girona, which he founded in 2014 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32714742/marc-gasol-play-spanish-club-girona-which-founded-2014 |access-date=November 25, 2021 |website=ESPN |date=November 25, 2021}}{{cite tweet |author=Bàsquet Girona |number=1463945092025274371 |title=🔙🏠 GIRONINES, GIRONINS, JA EL TENIM AQUÍ! 😍 📌 @MarcGasol, president del club, passa a formar part de la plantilla del primer equip 🙌 #CreixemJunts #SomhiGirona #OrgullGironí |user=BasquetGirona |date=November 25, 2021 |access-date=November 25, 2021 |language=Catalan}} He helped the team get [[Promotion and relegation|promoted]] to the [[Liga ACB]] for the first time, after Girona beat [[CB Estudiantes|Estudiantes]] 66–60 in the final of the promotion playoffs. Gasol added 11 points, 8 rebounds and 4 steals in the decisive final game.{{Cite web |date=2022-06-19 |title=Marc Gasol helps Girona earn promotion to ACB |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/acb/1359665/marc-gasol-girona-promoted-to-acb/ |access-date=2022-06-20 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}} Over the season, he averaged 14.5 points and 8.2 rebounds in 25 appearances for Girona. Gasol officially announced his retirement on January 31, 2024.{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Fappiano|title=Grizzlies legend Marc Gasol officially announces retirement from basketball|url=https://clutchpoints.com/grizzlies-news-marc-gasol-officially-announces-retirement-basketball|website=ClutchPoints.com|date=January 31, 2024|access-date=January 31, 2024}}{{cite web|title=Marc Gasol officially retires after 14 seasons|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39430033/marc-gasol-officially-retires-14-seasons|website=ESPN.com|date=January 31, 2024|access-date=January 31, 2024}} On April 6, 2024, the Grizzlies [[Retired number|retired]] his jersey number 33.{{Cite web |date=2024-04-07 |title=Grizzlies retire Marc Gasol's No. 33 jersey in postgame ceremony {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/grizzlies-marc-gasol-jersey-retirement |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=NBA |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2024-02-01 |title=Memphis Grizzlies plan to retire Marc Gasol's No. 33 jersey later this season |url=https://apnews.com/article/grizzlies-marc-gasol-292c3590ac889168a14c0e977f083786 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=AP News |language=en}} ==National team career== [[File:Gasol Brothers at the 2012 Summer Olympics.jpg|thumb|left|Marc and his brother Pau playing for [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain]] at the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]]]] In 2006, Gasol was named to the [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain national team]] for the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]] in Japan as a replacement for NBA-draftee [[Fran Vázquez]]. Spain went on to win the gold medal in Japan, as well as at the [[EuroBasket 2009]]. He also won silver medals at the [[EuroBasket 2007]], the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]], and the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]]. He won his second world championship title with the Spanish team at the [[2019 FIBA World Championship]] in China. He also won the gold medal at the [[EuroBasket 2011]], and bronze medals at the [[EuroBasket 2013]] and the [[EuroBasket 2017]]. At the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], Gasol won his second World Cup title.{{cite web |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/news/spain-recapture-fiba-basketball-world-cup-title-in-china |title=Spain recapture FIBA Basketball World Cup title in China |work=FIBA.basketball |date=September 15, 2019 |access-date=September 17, 2019}} Gasol scored 33 points in the semi-final to defeat [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australia]]. He scored 14 points, had a team-high 7 assists, had 2 steals, and blocked 3 shots in the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|Final]] against [[Argentina men's national basketball team|Argentina]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/en/more-sports/2019/09/15/5d7e4cf846163f8f878b45d0.html |title=Spain seal second FIBA World Cup with win over Argentina |date=September 15, 2019 |website=MARCA in English |access-date=September 15, 2019}} He was named to the World Cup All-Star Team along with teammate [[Ricky Rubio]].{{Cite web |date=September 15, 2019 |title=TISSOT Most Valuable Player Rubio headlines the All-Star Five |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/news/tissot-most-valuable-player-rubio-headlines-the-all-star-five |access-date=September 15, 2019 |publisher=FIBA}} Gasol became the second player in history to win an NBA championship and a World Cup in the same year, and the first non-American to win an NBA or WNBA title and either a World Cup or Olympic gold medal in the same year.{{Cite web |last=Reynolds |first=Tim |date=September 15, 2019 |title=Gasol completes historic double, Spain wins World Cup |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/gasol-completes-historic-double-spain-wins-world-cup-140648048--nba.html |access-date=September 15, 2019 |website=sports.yahoo.com |archive-date=October 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191005150201/https://sports.yahoo.com/gasol-completes-historic-double-spain-wins-world-cup-140648048--nba.html |url-status=dead }} After the Spanish Basketball Team fell to the [[United States men's national basketball team]] by a score of 81–95 in the [[2020 Summer Olympic Games]], Marc and his brother [[Pau Gasol]] announced they were retiring from the Spanish national team. This was the informal end to an unprecedented era of success for the Spanish team.{{cite web |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/juegos-olimpicos/20210803/1001670699/pau-marc-gasol-ponen-sueno-dorado-espana.html |title=Pau y Marc Gasol ponen fin al largo sueño dorado de España |publisher=Mundo Deportivo |language=ES |date=August 3, 2021 |access-date=August 3, 2021|trans-quote=Pau and Marc Gasol announced after the match their retirement from the Spanish team, which lowers a curtain on its brightest era in its history. Without the Gasol brothers and with many of their teammates on this journey clearly above the age of 30 (Rudy Fernández, Sergio Rodríguez, Sergio Llull, Victor Claver), Spanish basketball witnesses in Tokyo 2020 the end of a golden dream that has lasted for two decades, that of the elder Gasol who has helmed this team since that long-ago international debut in the Eurobasket of Turkey 2001.|quote=Pau y Marc Gasol anunciaron tras el partido su retirada definitiva de la selección española, que ve así como se baja el telón a la época más brillante de su historia. Sin los hermanos Gasol y con muchos de sus compañeros en esta travesía claramente por encima de los 30 años (Rudy Fernández, Sergio Rodríguez, Sergio Llull, Víctor Claver), el basket español vive en Tokio 2020 el final de un sueño dorado que se ha prolongado durante dos décadas, la que se ha mantenido al timón de este equipo el mayor de los Gasol desde aquel lejano debut internacional en el
